Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max: Key highlights

Apple executive chairman Tim Cook has wished people around the world a happy Diwali, sharing a festive photograph on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) that he said was taken on an iPhone 18 Pro Max. In the post shared Cook wished users a joyful celebration and shared a striking image showing a woman’s hands holding bright diya amid festive decorations. “Happy Diwali to everyone celebrating around the world! May the light of this festival brighten your year ahead,” Cook wrote. He credited the photo to Gursimran Basra, with the caption “Shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max.”The post follows Apple’s usual practice of marking festivals with images made by users on iPhone, tying the greeting to the camera’s capabilities.The iPhone 18 Pro Max's camera system plays a central role in Apple's latest flagship experience, delivering impressive results across a wide range of lighting conditions. The device captures sharp details, natural colours and balanced dynamic range, whether shooting bright daylight scenes or challenging low-light environments illuminated only by festive diyas and decorative lights. Its advanced computational photography features help preserve highlights and shadow details while maintaining realistic skin tones.Enhanced Night mode, improved portrait photography and high-resolution image processing allow users to capture professional-looking photos with minimal effort, making the iPhone 18 Pro Max a capable tool for everything from everyday snapshots to festival and travel photography.StorageIndia Price256GBRs 1,64,900512GBRs 1,89,9001TBRs 2,39,9002TBRs 3,14,900Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max: India price and availabilityDisplay: Both models feature Super Retina XDR displays with ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness. The Dynamic Island has been redesigned to take up less space while showing more information, including up to three Live Activities at once.Cameras: The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, bringing manual aperture control to the iPhone for the first time. The six-blade system offers four aperture settings and can automatically adjust based on lighting and depth of field. These phones also get upgraded Photographic Styles, Pro controls for settings such as shutter speed and white balance, and a histogram for checking exposure. Apple Reference Image can create a reference version of a photo using signed sensor data to help determine whether an image has been edited. Video features include Cinematic effects after capture at up to 60fps, 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse and an updated Audio Mix.Performance: Both models are powered by Apple's 2nm A20 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine delivers twice the AI processing power. The phones also use a redesigned vapour chamber with three times more surface area than the previous generation, enabling up to 40 per cent higher sustained performance, according to Apple.Battery: The iPhone 18 Pro offers up to 36 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours. The iPhone 18 Pro can charge up to 50 per cent in around 15 minutes and wirelessly charge up to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. Apple says five minutes of wired charging on the iPhone 18 Pro Max provides around seven hours of video playback, while the phone can offer up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge based on its new battery usage model.Software: Both phones ship with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Siri AI can use personal context from messages, emails and photos, understand onscreen content and help users find information or perform actions. iOS 27 also introduces iPhone Handoff, allowing users with supported carriers to switch between two iPhone models using the same phone number.Connectivity: The iPhone 18 Pro models feature Apple's N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. They also introduce the C2 cellular modem system, which Apple says provides faster uploads than C1X while consuming 15 per cent less energy.
Article Summary: Apple executive chairman Tim Cook has wished people around the world a happy Diwali. He shared a festive photograph on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) that he said was taken on an iPhone 18 Pro Max. The post follows Apple’s usual practice of marking festivals with images made by users on iPhone.

Article Title: Experts in Canada are testing doorbell cameras' for Polar bears, called Bear-vision, they combine radar and cameras to …
Article Text:
Image Credit: Alan Wilson/Wikipedia

How will Bear-vision work

Why is Churchill’s waste facility the first location

Why are bears spending longer near communities

What other tools are researchers testing

“It’s not easy to live with large predators as your neighbours, so we’re investing in coexistence approaches, especially as we see climate change causing more human-bear encounters. By developing and field-testing innovative, non-lethal deterrents like drones and detection tech like Bear-vision, we’re hoping to expand the variety of safe, effective, and affordable coexistence tools available to communities,”

Researchers are testing Bear-vision cameras to warn communities in Canada about approaching polar bears. Conservation charity Polar Bears International is developing Bear-vision, a warning system built on security camera technology that can be paired with shorter-range radar. Its first deployment is planned at Churchill’s waste facility this autumn to help monitor bears and reduce surprise encounters, the organisation’ noted in a blog post.The camera is intended to offer a more affordable, easy-to-use alternative to wide-area radar systems. Researchers will use data gathered at the site to train it to recognise polar bears and send notifications when they appear. The project comes as bears gather along Hudson Bay, waiting for sea ice to return so they can hunt seals, while communities work to keep people and wildlife safely apart.Bear-vision builds on the organisation’s earlier Bear-dar detection work. While Bear-dar monitors wider areas using radar, the new system uses smart security camera technology and can incorporate shorter-range radar.​Polar Bears International compares the intended function to a doorbell camera that alerts residents when a polar bear is outside. The Churchill deployment will help researchers gather the information needed to train the notification system.Churchill began working with Polar Bears International to keep bears out of its dump after a fire destroyed its waste facilities. Garbage can attract bears looking for food, creating risks for both the animals and people nearby.The response includes new electric fences, Bear-dar and Bear-vision monitoring, and a visit by a Churchill delegation to a waste management facility in Greenland. The camera trial is part of a broader effort to manage the site, not replace physical barriers or other measures.Polar Bears International says climate-driven sea ice loss leaves bears waiting on land about a month longer than their grandparents did. The ice-free period around Hudson Bay now lasts three to four weeks longer than in the 1980s, placing additional strain on their stored fat reserves.The organisation says these longer periods ashore make coexistence measures increasingly important. Its Polar Bear Week, running November 1–7, coincides with the seasonal gathering near Churchill.Polar Bears International and Brigham Young University are also working with Churchill’s Polar Bear Alert Program to test drones as an affordable, non-lethal way to move bears away from communities. That separate deterrent project includes ultrasonic sound, conductive materials and a new odour-based bear spray formula.said Geoff York, Polar Bears International’s vice president of science and policy.
Article Summary: Polar Bears International is developing Bear-vision, a warning system built on security camera technology that can be paired with shorter-range radar. Its first deployment is planned at Churchill’s waste facility this autumn. Researchers will use data gathered at the site to train it to recognise polar bears and send notifications when they appear.

Article Title: Meet Donovan Atkinson, the 5-year-old who turned cucumbers from his family's garden into a pickle business and sold more than 500 jars from his roadside stand
Article Text:
PC: Facebook

How Donovan and his mother turned cucumbers into pickles

More than 500 jars sold under The Pickle Kid name

What running a pickle stand is teaching the five-year-old

The five-year-old has bigger plans for his pickle venture

A roadside stand selling homemade pickles is not the usual sight associated with a five-year-old. Yet Donovan Atkinson, a young boy from Attleboro, Massachusetts, has found himself running just such a venture, with cucumbers from his family's garden providing the starting point. What began with a surplus of home-grown vegetables eventually developed into a small business, complete with its own name, customers and jars carrying a distinctive label. Known locally as 'The Pickle Kid', Donovan has already sold more than 500 jars since setting up his stand in 2025. His experience has also introduced him to some of the everyday responsibilities involved in selling a product.The idea came about after Donovan's family grew more cucumbers than they could readily use in their garden. Rather than letting the extra produce go to waste, he and his mother, Gabrielle Atkinson, started experimenting with making pickles at home.The kitchen became the first place where the project took shape. Donovan worked alongside his mother, turning the garden harvest into jars of pickled cucumbers. For Donovan, the process offered a way to do something with the vegetables he had helped grow. It also gave the family an idea that could extend beyond their own kitchen.In 2025, Donovan took the next step and opened a roadside pickle stand. The small venture gave him an opportunity to sell the jars to people outside his immediate family and circle of friends.The response was enough to turn the project into a growing local activity. More than 500 jars have since been sold, with customers including neighbours, friends and people who happened to pass by the stand.His business became known as ‘The Pickle Kid’, a name that reflects both his age and the product he sells. The nickname has also become part of the presentation, appearing on the jars themselves.Selling the jars has given Donovan some early experience with the practical side of running a business. Each sale involves more than handing over a product. He has opportunities to count money, speak with customers and become familiar with the small interactions that come with selling something to the public.His mother has been involved throughout the process, helping him make the pickles and supporting the activity as it developed. At his age, the business remains a family-supported undertaking, but Donovan has already become familiar with several aspects of customer service and basic money management.The experience has also helped him build confidence when dealing with people who visit the stand. These are skills that extend beyond the immediate business, even as the pickle sales remain the main focus.The roadside stand is only the beginning of what Donovan would like to achieve. According to the WCVB report, he hopes to develop The Pickle Kid into a full pickle business in the future. For now, the operation remains centred on the small-scale sales that grew out of his family's garden. There is no indication that the business has moved into wider commercial production, but the more than 500 jars already sold give an idea of how far the original project has travelled. At five, he is still at the beginning of his entrepreneurial experience. But The Pickle Kid already has a name, a roadside stand and a growing customer base.
Article Summary: Donovan Atkinson and his mother grew more cucumbers than they could use in their garden. The five-year-old started experimenting with making pickles in the kitchen. In 2025, he opened a roadside pickle stand in Attleboro, Massachusetts. More than 500 jars have already been sold, with customers including neighbours, friends and people who happened to pass by.

Article Title: Michigan evaluated centerline rumble strips across nearly 5,400 miles of rural roads; target crashes fell 47%, and target fatal crashes fell 51%
Article Text:
AI representation of road workers installing and inspecting centerline rumble strips on a rural two-lane highway, a safety measure designed to alert drivers when their vehicles drift across the centerline. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

How centerline rumble strips work

What the Michigan evaluation found

To boost road safety, the Michigan Department of Transportation has installed centerline rumble strips on rural roads, resulting in a 47% decrease in target crashes and a 51% decrease in fatalities. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

Research supports the wider use of rumble strips

One simple application of roadside safety innovations yielded strong outcomes across nearly 5,400 miles of rural roads in Michigan. Centerline rumble strips reduced target crashes by 47% and fatal crashes by 51%. The initiative, led by the Michigan Department of Transportation , emphasises control to avoid vehicles crossing the centerline into the traffic lane. The study compared crash data from the three years before and the three years after the improvements. The findings emphasised that modest improvements in road surfacing, which are relatively low cost, can make a difference for some of the worst crashes occurring on rural high-speed roads.Centreline rumble strips are small, shallow grooves that are cut into the pavement surface along the road centreline, generally under or near the centreline markings. Tires rolling across the grooves vibrate and rattle, and this sound and vibration notify drivers that their vehicle may be leaving the lane.The warning is most effective when the driver becomes distracted or tired and loses concentration for a time. Instead of having to spot the marking on the road themselves, the grooves act as a physical reminder for the driver to realign the steering before moving into the oncoming traffic lane.Rumble strips can be installed on existing roads as a post-construction road engineering measure, and they are seen as a relatively inexpensive option for roads where opposing traffic flows are not physically separated.MDOT initiated and completed the state-wide centerline rumble strip installation project between 2008 and 2010. The department installed the strips on rural non-freeway highways with a posted speed limit of 55 miles per hour. The project was 54 miles long, and shoulder rumble strips were also installed along some of the wider shoulders.The study considered 3 crash types: head-on crashes, side-swipe crashes between vehicles moving in opposite directions, and single-vehicle crashes where the driver departs the road to the left. The data reveal 2,488 target crashes for the before period and 1,306 in the after period. The study revealed a statistically significant reduction in all three types of crashes and a 51% decrease in fatalities within the target group.The researchers controlled for snowfall variation by excluding crashes in which snowy or icy pavement was noted as a contributing factor, reducing the chance that winter weather would distort the comparison. The researchers also show the programme's worth. Their benefit-cost ratio, ranging from 18:1 to 58:1 depending on the discount rate applied in the analysis, showed potential financial gain from preventing severe crashes far exceeded installation costs.Michigan's findings are consistent with research conducted in other parts of the United States. A study published in Accident Analysis & Prevention in 2025 examined centreline rumble strips on rural two-lane roads in Maine. It found reductions of between 28% and 48% in head-on, opposite-direction side-Y collisions, with an estimated benefit at least 14 times the installation cost. Another study published in the Journal of Transportation Engineering in 2016 examined the effectiveness of centreline and shoulder rumble strips on rural roads in Kentucky, Missouri, and Pennsylvania. Overall, the report detected A 36.8% reduction in head-on crashes, but the combined reduction in lane-departure crashes was a test assessed to be in the order of 27%Findings from the studies suggest that Rumble strips can provide quantifiable safety benefits for various types of road systems, but rumble strips do not work equally well on all roads, with the design of installation and the type of crashes targeted as factors. The program also showed how safety can integrate into the day-to-day work of road maintenance, and Michigan MDOT is transitioning to a contract for annual payment, marking a more efficient installation process and eliminating the need for dedicated construction projects.
Article Summary: Centerline rumble strips are small, shallow grooves that are cut into the pavement surface along the road centreline. Tires rolling across the grooves vibrate and rattle, and this sound and vibration notify drivers that their vehicle may be leaving the lane. The warning is most effective when the driver becomes distracted or tired and loses concentration for a time.

Article Title: A Hertfordshire couple used an inherited Chinese brush pot as a doorstop for 40 years; experts identified the late 18th- or early 19th-century carving, which sold for a £150,000 hammer price
Article Text:
Representative AI image of an intricately carved Chinese wooden brush pot that remained an ordinary household doorstop for decades before its historical and artistic value was recognised. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

An overlooked object comes to light

The craft and meaning behind a Chinese brush

An intricately carved 18th-century Chinese bamboo brush pot, similar to the antique inherited by a Hertfordshire couple, who used it as a doorstop for 40 years before it sold for £150,000. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

A £150,000 reminder of hidden heritage

A Chinese antique worth £250,000 spent 40 years doing an everyday household chore in a Hertfordshire cottage. Its owners, who inherited it, used it as a doorstop, not knowing the carved wooden ornament was a valuable example of traditional Chinese craftsmanship. The auctioneer, called in to value the family's other possessions, recognised the object as a calligrapher's brush pot carved from zitan wood and decorated with the Hundred Boys motif, dating to the late 18th or early 19th century. Antiques Trade Gazette reported it sold at Sworders' Asian art sale in May 2014.The pair inherited the brush pot and kept it at their home for nearly 40 years. They propped it in the doorway to a sitting room as a doorstop. Its importance was realised when an auctioneer visited to assess the rest of the cottage's contents. The brush pot intrigued Richard Harrison, who recognised it as an 18th-century Chinese carving, which was to become a major feature of an Asian art sale.It was a carved Zitan wood ‘Hundred Boys’ biotong, or brush pot, by Sworders, measuring approximately 2.45 cm high; it was dated to the late 18th/early 19th century.It was hammered at £150,000 in April 2014. It was a “famous and important” lot which Sworders believed would have excellent prospects. There were dozens of small boys carved into the lively design, and a report of the sale quoted Harrison as describing the figure as 'almost three-dimensional' and 'doing all sorts of things,' notably 'setting off firecrackers'. He also commented on the remarkable condition of the object, which had been used for many years as a doorstop.A bitong is the Chinese term for a brush pot. They were placed on the desk alongside writers' or painters' brushes and tools. They served an everyday utilitarian function but also displayed dexterity and art. Unlike the other writing instruments kept in the scholar's studio, the brush pot was the vessel that was merely functional. The tools of writing and painting defined the scholar's studio, where brushes and ink stones were kept, and the owner's taste was displayed. The barrel-shaped vessel was carved with an inviting little scene to be examined up close: the Hundred Boys motif symbolised good luck and prosperity for offspring. Carved brush pots were made from many materials, from bamboo and wood, but Chinese furniture makers and carvers especially prized zitan as it was a dense, very desirable timber with tightly grained and dark coloured.Academic research helps explain why these objects deserve attention beyond their practical purpose. A study in Arte Individuo y Sociedad examines Chinese curved bamboo stationery, connecting decorative models with painting and literacy culture research published in Trans/ Form/ Acao , brings together the carved brush pot and closely examines the Hertfordshire example to show how the carved brush conveyed the language of a spatialisation found in landscape painting in three dimensions. The piece is carved from Zitan wood rather than bamboo, but these studies give insight into the artistic aspiration of a scholar's object.The sale also reinforces how valuable expert knowledge is when it comes to spotting antiques. Without the visit, the pot would have been just a hard-to-ship paperweight. Sworders, based in Stansted Mountfitchet, Essex, established a specialist Asian art department and drew in collectors from markets such as Hong Kong and Mainland China, and the auction house later described the brush pot as one of the leading Chinese art sales.£150,000 was the hammer price, not what was paid after the premium. To the couple, The Hunt started as part of a normal valuation of household contents and finished as the realisation that an heirloom had travelled through one of the most prominent artistic circles in the world.
Article Summary: A Chinese antique worth £250,000 spent 40 years doing an everyday household chore in a Hertfordshire cottage. Its owners, who inherited it, used it as a doorstop, not knowing the carved wooden ornament was a valuable example of traditional Chinese craftsmanship. It was a carved Zitan wood ‘Hundred Boys’ biotong, or brush pot, measuring approximately 2.45 cm high; it was dated to the late 18th/early 19th century.

Article Title: Cancer patient came up with a fundraising idea at his kitchen table during treatment; 21 years later, his UK platform has raised more than £50 million for charities
Article Text:
PC: Easyfundraising

How did a cancer patient develop the fundraising idea during treatment

Easyfundraising turns online shopping into charitable fundraising

How can shoppers support charities without spending extra money

How does easyfundraising help charities and good causes of all sizes

An idea formed during cancer treatment and worked out at a kitchen table has become one of the UK’s biggest charity shopping platforms. Ian Woodroffe founded easyfundraising after seeing a chance to join charitable fundraising to the UK’s growing e-commerce industry. It launched officially in 2005. Supporters raise money for charities and good causes just by shopping online through participating brands, so they never make a separate donation. The company’s website says easyfundraising has now raised over £50 million for more than 180,000 charities and good causes across the UK.The idea originated during a conversation at a New Year's Eve party in 2002. However, it was during his cancer treatment that founder Ian Woodroffe developed the concept of connecting fundraising with the growing UK e-commerce sector.The company explains that Woodroffe had developed a new understanding of the importance of fundraising for charities and good causes during a critical period in his life. This experience inspired him to create an accessible way for people to support charitable organisations. His vision was to establish an easy and free fundraising method that would help causes receive much-needed financial support. The concept also reflected his belief that everyday online shopping could become an opportunity to make a positive difference.By allowing shoppers to raise donations without paying anything extra, Woodroffe aimed to remove financial barriers to charitable giving. This approach eventually helped turn an ordinary consumer activity into a practical fundraising opportunity for charities across the UK.The idea was developed around Woodroffe's kitchen table before easyfundraising officially launched in 2005. The platform was built around the concept of combining online shopping with charitable fundraising, allowing people to support causes through purchases they were already making.Easyfundraising was established to provide a free way for charities and good causes across the UK to raise funds. Rather than requiring supporters to make additional donations, its model connects online shoppers with brands that give back to their chosen causes through the platform.The platform has raised more than £50 million for over 180,000 charities and good causes since its launch. Its model works by connecting supporters who want to contribute to charitable organisations with participating brands that provide donations through online shopping.The company describes its mission as turning everyday spending into a force for good. People can choose a cause they want to support, browse participating brands and shop online through easyfundraising. The platform provides a way to generate funds for their chosen causes through these purchases without requiring shoppers to donate additional money themselves.Easyfundraising aims to make fundraising technology accessible to charities and good causes of all sizes. Its platform supports a range of organisations, from local football teams and children's schools to national charities. The company says its mission is to provide technology that makes fundraising easier and helps organisations continue their work.Its purpose is to make giving part of everyday life rather than a separate activity. With an expanding list of participating brands, easyfundraising continues to connect shoppers, businesses and charitable organisations through its online platform. Its stated mission is to help people turn ordinary spending into financial support for the causes they care about.
Article Summary: Easyfundraising was established to provide a free way for charities and good causes across the UK to raise funds. Rather than requiring supporters to make additional donations, its model connects online shoppers with brands that give back to their chosen causes through the platform. The platform has raised more than £50 million for over 180,000 charities since its launch in 2005.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

Is Aadhaar mandatory for a digital Life Certificate



Legal validity of Jeevan Pramaan



How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: CERT-In seeks checks on access of AI agents
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: India's cybersecurity agency has called for testing whether AI agents can leak confidential data or take unauthorised actions, putting permissions and human oversight at the centre of its audit guidelines.CERT-In's AI Security Auditing Guidelines, dated Nov 4, specify limits on agents' access to business systems, records of their actions and emergency interruption mechanisms for high-risk deployments. Agents "shall not automatically inherit permissions from users, tools or other agents", the guidelines stated. The safeguards address prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in documents or other inputs attempt to hijack an AI system's behaviour."Consequential actions shall use appropriate human approval gates," the guidelines noted. Auditors should test whether these approvals can be bypassed and whether authorised reviewers can reject, correct or override AI outputs. The framework also calls for testing safeguards against data leaks.
Article Summary: India's cybersecurity agency has called for testing whether AI agents can leak confidential data or take unauthorised actions. CERT-In's AI Security Auditing Guidelines specify limits on agents' access to business systems. The safeguards address prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in documents or other inputs attempt to hijack an AI system's behaviour.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, who famously warned internet has become ‘less human’, now says AI ‘can cause a lot of harm’
Article Text:
Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian

The age of 'AI Slop' and dead internet

Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian believes the internet as we know it is fundamentally broken, and artificial intelligence (AI) is both a symptom and a driver of the shift. Speaking with WIRED at the inaugural WIRED World Fair recently, Ohanian warned that while AI holds massive promise, “there is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure. ” Ohanian also said that building traditional social media apps is “not cool anymore”, as much of the web has been compromised, leaving him searching for what comes next for user-generated content (UGC).Ohanian now leads the venture capital firm Seven Seven Six, which manages over $1.3 billion in assets. Lately, he has turned his attention to sports, an area where he still sees genuine, real-life communities thriving “in the age of AI slop” and a “manipulated” internet. He is an open proponent of the “Dead Internet Theory,” the idea that bots now generate a massive share of online content and activity. According to Ohanian, large language models have put this trend into overdrive, with AI agents rapidly outpacing real people.“The internet that I grew up on … that was really built for humans first; user interfaces and experiences are going to go away,” Ohanian said, explaining that the web is increasingly being built for AI agents rather than human users.The boom in generative AI has created a complicated reality for platforms like Reddit. On one hand, Reddit’s massive archive of human conversations has become a goldmine, leading to lucrative data-licensing deals with companies like Google and OpenAI to train their models. “Platforms like ours became very, very valuable to LLMs,” Ohanian noted.On the other hand, the technology is \ undercutting the business. Just last week, Reddit’s shares dropped 29% after the company warned that Google’s AI-powered search was eating into its referral traffic. Beyond the stock price, Ohanian worries that turning online discussions into a commercial product has ruined their authenticity, leaving them full of “bullshit.”“The internet has gotten so manipulated because it is so incredibly valuable to do so,” he said.To combat third-party data scraping and protect user engagement, Reddit recently announced it will require users to sign in. While Ohanian declined to say whether he supports that specific policy, he stressed that “there has to be provable humanity on the internet without being creepy.”
Article Summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian believes the internet as we know it is fundamentally broken. He believes artificial intelligence (AI) is both a symptom and a driver of the shift. Ohanian warned that while AI holds massive promise, “there is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure”

Article Title: As $2.5 billion transferred from Binance in single transaction; how it cost hackers just $15; the massive cryptocurrency theft’s ‘big shock’
Article Text:
Cryptocurrency theft

How a ‘$15 transaction’ that cleared the vault

It took hackers just $15 to unlock access to $2.5 billion, followed by a matter of seconds to move the entire sum, to pull off the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. That striking reality sits at the center of the historic cryptocurrency theft from Binance, where attackers leveraged an advanced Ethereum feature to siphon roughly 40% of their total haul in one single transaction. This incident was part of a broader, sophisticated cyberattack that drained an estimated $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance, according to Bloomberg. The FBI has tied the breach to North Korea.Binance disclosed that the breach began when an engineer fell for a fake job posting and downloaded malicious code, granting the hackers entry into internal systems. What followed was a high-level exploitation of Ethereum’s underlying mechanics that allowed the intruders to move billions even while the exchange scrambled to lock down its operations.The central target was Binance 14, an active hot wallet used by the platform to handle regular customer withdrawals. Connected directly to online services, the wallet held massive balances of Ether, stablecoins and dozens of alternative tokens. Having breached Binance’s signing infrastructure, the attackers secured a valid cryptographic signature from the Binance 14 wallet. At around 8:20 p.m. UTC on October 29, they broadcasted instructions to the Ethereum network, paying roughly $15 in standard network gas fees.That $15 transaction did not move any cryptocurrency. Instead, it registered authorisation for the hackers' own software to operate the wallet.The negligible cost highlights how public blockchains function: Ethereum processing fees reflect the computational effort needed to run a piece of code and overall network demand – not the monetary value of the tokens inside an account. Modifying access rights on an account holding billions costs the exact same as doing so on an account holding a few dollars.Approximately three and a half minutes later, the attackers triggered their software to execute a single, sweeping transfer worth roughly $2.5 billion.The fast drain was caused by EIP-7702, an Ethereum improvement proposal introduced on May 7, 2025, during the network’s Pectra upgrade.Available for about 18 months, EIP-7702 was designed to streamline the user experience by giving standard crypto wallets programmable capabilities, like bundling multiple separate operations into a single step or allowing third parties to cover transaction fees. In everyday terms, it acts like appointing a concierge authorised to handle multiple errands without requiring sign-off on every task.Security analysts point out that EIP-7702 did not open the door on its own; the hackers had already infiltrated Binance's systems and compromised its signing credentials. However, the feature allowed the attackers' code to step directly into Binance 14's shoes.By using EIP-7702's bundling capabilities, the hackers consolidated the withdrawal into a single transaction that cleared 167,464 Ether, over 60 other cryptocurrencies, including roughly $1.6 billion worth of Tether (USDT) – the combined haul totaled approximately $2.5 billion.
Article Summary: Hackers used advanced feature to siphon roughly 40% of total haul in one transaction. Incident was part of a broader, sophisticated cyberattack that drained an estimated $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance. FBI has tied the breach to North Korea.

Article Title: After reported cases of broken bones, brain damage and other injuries; US Consumer Product Safety Commission issues red alert; tells Lowe’s, Costco and Amazon to recall 3.6 million …
Article Text:
Pic courtesy: US Consumer Product Safety Commission website

What US CPSC 'red notice' says

Which ladder models are being recalled

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has issued an alert notifying consumers across America that 3.6 million ladders are being recalled because they could unexpectedly retract due to faulty locks. According to reports, warning comes after a number of people sustained broken bones, brain damage and other injuries.US CPSC has published a recall notice warning consumers that approximately 3,662,000 (3.6 million) ladders made by Little Giant Ladder Systems were being recalled after the company received several reports of the ladders unexpectedly retracting, causing serious injuries to users. As per CPSC's warning to buyers: "Ladders can suddenly retract if the Rapid Locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard to consumers. "The faulty ladders have been sold on Lowes, Amazon, Costco, LittleGiantLadders and other websites. As per the consumer body, the 3.6 million-plus ladders included in this recall were sold nationally between December 2015 and October 2026. The ladders sold are priced anywhere from around $100 to around $1,000.The CPSC's notice says that the Rapid Locks are black or orange components on the ladders’ legs, designed to be inserted to adjust the ladders’ height.When the Rapid Locks don’t work as intended, the ladders can suddenly retract, causing the user to fall and sustain serious injuries. Little Giant has also published its own recall notice, in which the ladder manufacturer warns of the same hazard."Consumers should stop using the recalled ladders immediately until they review the information at http://www.littlegiantladders.com/pages/recalls or via the QR code on the ladder and contact Little Giant for a repair kit containing warning labels and instructions. The additional instructions and labels, which should be affixed to the ladder, advise consumers to verify that their Rapid Locks are properly engaged before every use and to maintain their locks with lubrication. Consumers who follow the provided instructions and have a Rapid Lock that does not function properly after the application of lubrication should contact Little Giant for evaluation. If a lock does not function properly after this evaluation, the company will offer the choice of a replacement ladder of the same or equivalent model or a refund ranging from a depreciated value determined by date of purchase up to full purchase price for ladders purchased within the past 12 months," said the USCPC on its page.The CPSC says the following models of Little Giant ladders are being recalled: Adjustable Fortress 2.0, Conquest 2.0, Dark Horse 2.0, Epic, King Kombo XT, Leveler, MegaLite, MegaLite+, Multi, Quantum and Vector.

Article Title: Goldman Sachs bans thousands of employees from using Claude Code and GitHub; company says: After a period of experimentation, we put them in the hands of those...
Article Text:
No more vibe coding for Goldman traders

Goldman's CIO was cheering vibe coding by traders in July

Goldman's AI policy reflects a wider Wall Street rethink

Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its staff from advanced AI coding tools, and not everyone at the bank is pleased. Access to tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub is now limited to engineers, according to internal guidance updated in October and seen by Bloomberg. Traders, bankers and other non-technical employees, many of whom had been using these tools for months, have lost access.The bank says the call came after it looked at productivity and risk. A Goldman spokesperson, Nick Carcaterra, told Bloomberg that the firm offers certain AI tools to staff so it can figure out where they work best. Once that trial period ends, the tools go "in the hands of those who are best suited to leverage them," he said.There is one exception. The rule does not apply to strats, Goldman's term for employees who sit between trading, quantitative research and software engineering.Traders seem to feel the change most. According to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg, some had been using the tools to track client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and put together written and graphic content. On a trading desk, losing that kind of speed is felt quickly.The reversal stands out because Goldman had been openly encouraging this. In July, chief information officer Marco Argenti spoke about vibe coding by traders and bankers. He described non-technical staff building their own fixes with AI and passing them to one of the firm's 12,000 engineers to refine.This is also not Goldman's first AI restriction. Earlier this year, the bank limited the use of Anthropic's Claude for its Hong Kong staff, though that rule applied only to that location.None of this means Goldman is stepping back from AI. It has built an in-house AI assistant that combines models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google parent Alphabet. In May, John Waldron, seen as the likely successor to CEO David Solomon, compared the bank to an assembly line run by people and said much of that work could be automated.Goldman isn't the only bank rethinking how its staff use AI. Firms across Wall Street are spending millions of dollars on these tools while also dealing with cybersecurity worries, rising bills and uneven productivity gains. Working out who should use what has become a task of its own.JPMorgan Chase said in July it wanted employees to match models to tasks, so the priciest option isn't used for something as basic as summarising an analyst report. The idea is to keep costs in check without slowing people down.Goldman's move follows a similar line, applied to coding assistants. Instead of opening every tool to every employee, the bank is deciding which roles need them and limiting access to those roles.For now, that means engineers and strats. The traders who had built daily workflows around Claude Code and GitHub will have to find another way to get that work done.
Article Summary: Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its staff from advanced AI coding tools. Access to tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub is now limited to engineers. Traders, bankers and other non-technical employees have lost access. Goldman says the call came after it looked at productivity and risk.

Article Title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal answers why he left his $35 billion company for Temple: A weekend project while I was still Zomato CEO ended in…
Article Text:
Deepinder Goyal explains why he left Zomato for Temple

Deepinder Goyal built Temple around his dislike of AI devices

Goyal answers doctors’ criticism with $20 million of his own money

Deepinder Goyal says Temple was never meant to be his next big bet. In a vision note titled “Humanity’s Last Personal Device”, the Zomato founder writes that he began building a health wearable as a weekend project while he was still CEO of Eternal, the company formerly known as Zomato. That project led to an engineering breakthrough, and the breakthrough is what pulled him out of Eternal to build Temple full-time.The note answers a question Goyal raised himself on X earlier in the day. Many people, he wrote, wanted to know why he would leave a roughly $35 billion company he founded 18 years ago to chase a niche health wearable. He conceded that it doesn’t sound like a rational move.Goyal’s reasoning starts with a grievance. He argues that privacy is a basic human right, and that every voice AI device sold as the next computing interface breaks it the moment its microphone switches on, because a mic records everyone in the room. He writes that he hates it when people walk into meetings with him with their AI note-taker running.Temple is his workaround. Instead of a mic, it reads the vibrations of the wearer’s voice through motion sensors, so it hears the person wearing it and nobody else. Goyal wrote, with an expletive, that there wasn’t even a word for that, so Temple invented one: “roomdeaf”.He is just as particular about what Temple won’t do. Goyal calls it a companion and not an assistant, because it will not shop for you and will stick to tasks that don’t need a screen.Personal devices, in his view, should get out of the way. He also writes that he sees Temple serving humanity in the space age, and suggests a few Black Mirror episodes as a reference for where it could go.Not everyone is sold. A section of Indian doctors has questioned Temple’s health claims on X, and Goyal replied with a seven-point post addressed to them.His first argument was commercial. Temple offers 14-day, no-questions-asked returns, which he noted even Apple doesn’t offer in India, so a device that failed to deliver would be exposed within days. He said Temple has cost $30 million so far, $20 million of it his own, and that a few thousand units would recover only a fraction of that. A scam that pays nothing, he wrote, isn’t one anyone would run.Then he made it personal. Goyal said he has enough money to last generations and would not stake a reputation built over 20 years on a quick buck. Temple’s employees invested in a round a few months ago, he added, and the round being raised now is mostly made up of customers.On the science, he pointed to Whoop, which shipped its band in 2015 and published validation a few years later. Temple’s pre-prints are coming, Goyal said, and its most groundbreaking features are still under wraps. He signed off by telling the doctors to keep raging if he hadn’t convinced them.Goyal calls Temple “a project, not a product” and says health remains its north star. Temple 01 ships in early 2027 with both AI and health features, pre-orders are open, and he is already talking about what Temple 20 might look like.The move he admits doesn’t look rational now has his money and a 20-year reputation riding on it.
Article Summary: Deepinder Goyal built Temple around his dislike of AI devices. Goyal says he has enough money to last generations and would not stake a reputation built over 20 years on a quick buck. Temple 01 ships in early 2027 with both AI and health features, pre-orders are open.

Article Title: Google faces what may be the first lawsuit over AI on school laptops
Article Text:
Parents say Google’s AI Mode put their daughter at risk

Google Search pulled her into AI Mode, the family claims

Schools can switch off Gemini, but not the AI inside Google Search

A 13-year-old’s parents have sued Google , claiming its artificial intelligence pushed their daughter towards planning her own death after months of chats on a school-issued Chromebook. The case, filed in California Superior Court on Monday, is likely the first to accuse Google of rushing AI into apps on K-12 school laptops without warning parents, The New York Times reported.The complaint calls the girl Emma, a seventh grader in Charlotte, North Carolina. Her parents, named John and Jane Doe, say they learned she could access Google’s AI only in mid-March, when her school warned she was in “imminent danger” of self-harm. Her mother logged into Emma’s school Google account and found she had been writing about ending her life in Google Docs. Emma was rushed for an emergency psychiatric evaluation and now sees a therapist weekly.According to the lawsuit, Emma had limited access to laptops at home and never set out to use Google’s AI. As she searched the web on her school device, Google “routed” her to AI Mode, the chatbot-like feature built into Search.By March, she was exchanging thousands of messages with it late into the night, picking the chats back up as soon as she woke. The complaint alleges the AI told Emma she had major mental illnesses, persuaded her to trust it over her parents and counsellors, and helped her plan her suicide and funeral.Google’s systems did not alert her school or parents. The warning came from a separate monitoring company the school used, which scans student writing on school devices for signs of self-harm.Google spokesperson José Castañeda said the crisis hotline details it has long shown in Search, built with health experts, also appear in its AI search features. Google is reviewing the claims.The lawsuit argues that Google’s spread of Chromebooks and school apps let it push Gemini into public schools, sometimes switching student access on by default. Administrators can toggle apps like YouTube and Gemini by grade, but have complained that AI Mode and AI Overviews in Search cannot be disabled.The filing lands in the same week Google said it would turn off Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search by default for K-12 schools in early 2027. Schools that bring Search back must choose between the regular AI-powered version and one built on Guided Learning, a step-by-step tutoring mode. There is no option without AI. “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told NYT.The plan drew quick criticism. Senator Bernie Sanders called it “extortion,” while former FTC chair Lina Khan accused Google of using its search monopoly to coerce schools. Google said on X that the changes give schools “more choice, not less.” The move also reverses an August change that turned on Gemini in Classroom for students of all ages.The case adds to mounting legal pressure on Big Tech over young users. Meta recently agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion to settle claims from 47 states over addictive features, though it denies wrongdoing.Emma’s family says she never went looking for Google’s AI. Under the 2027 plan, students in any school that keeps Search will still find it there.
Article Summary: Parents say Google’s AI Mode put their daughter at risk. Google is reviewing the claims. The case adds to mounting legal pressure on Big Tech over young users. Google recently announced it would turn off Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search by default for K-12 schools in early 2027.

Article Title: How to level up your Diwali lighting game with smart lights and strips
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

Start with a lighting plan for each space

Use LED strips to create a glow around decorations

Choose colour around the occasion

Check what makes the light 'smart'

Create settings for puja, guests and bedtime

Give outdoor lighting a separate check

Plan a role for the lights after Diwali

Diwali lighting should have a purpose. For example, you could use warm lighting at the entrance to welcome visitors, concealed lights for decorations, and stored scenes to shift the living room's atmosphere from puja to dinner.Smart lights add control to that setup, letting compatible bulbs and strips change brightness, colour, or operating hours. However, an effective setup starts with placement and planning. For a compact flat, start with one illuminated entrance, one softly lit gathering space, and one decorative highlight. This gives the home distinct points of interest while leaving room for diyas, flowers and rangoli to remain part of the display.Before choosing lights, decide how you'll use each area. The entrance needs enough illumination for guests to see the doorway and move comfortably. The living room needs light for conversations, serving sweets and taking photographs. Decorative corners can use softer accents.A practical arrangement could combine a warm bulb near the entrance, an LED strip behind a living-room cabinet and a separate light directed towards a festive display.This approach also gives existing lights a role. A ceiling light can provide general illumination when needed, while the decorative layers create the evening setting. You don't need to replace every bulb or outline every surface for the arrangement to feel different.LED strips offer several placement options, but the effect depends on where you place them. A visible strip creates a defined line of light. A concealed strip directs attention towards the surface it illuminates.Behind a sideboard, beneath a shelf or inside a ceiling recess, a strip can create a background glow around festive decorations. Along a window frame, it can give the display a clearer outline. Choosing one or two such features can help keep the room visually balanced.Plan the installation before you remove the adhesive backing. Measure the intended route, identify the nearest socket and check where the cable and power adapter will sit. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions on mounting, ventilation and whether the strip can be cut or extended.Colour-changing lights offer room to experiment, but a consistent palette can make the decorations feel more connected.Warm white or gold can form the background around flowers, lanterns and the puja area. A separate coloured accent behind the seating space can introduce a different mood for an evening gathering.Steady lighting is a useful starting point. Try colour cycles and animated effects in a smaller area before adding them to the full display. That makes it easier to judge whether the effect suits the room and the people using it.Brightness deserves the same attention. Decorative lights should complement the room’s general illumination, while leaving enough light around steps, doorways, and serving areas.An LED strip is not smart by default. Some products offer a fixed colour; others change colours via a remote control or app.Before you buy, ask a few simple questions: Does the light allow dimming, colour changes, schedules and saved settings? Can I control more than one light at a time? Do you need a separate device to control by voice?It's better to check compatibility with the household’s router and control devices, as some smart lights require additional hardware. It also notes that most need standby power to remain controllable. Switching them off at the wall can therefore affect app-based operationWhere supported, a lighting “scene” saves several choices so you can recall them together. Instead of adjusting each light separately, the household can select a setting prepared for the occasion.A puja scene could combine warm, steady lighting with a subdued background. A gathering scene could brighten the seating area and add colour behind a cabinet. A bedtime scene could switch off the decorative lights together.Schedules can handle another part of the routine by turning compatible lights on and off at selected times. Features vary between products, so test the full setup before the celebrations. Another household member should also know how to operate it.Balconies, terraces, and entrances need products suited to their installation conditions. Don't assume an indoor strip is suitable for an exposed railing just because it uses LEDs.The rating and instructions for the complete setup matter, including the adapter, connections and extension cord. The Electrical Safety Foundation International advises using appropriately rated cords, avoiding overloads and switching off electrical decorations before leaving home or going to bed.Timers can help establish that routine, but you still need to check the setup in person. Keep cables out of the way of people walking past, and keep electric lights and connections away from open flames.The most useful placement is often one that works beyond the festival. A concealed living-room strip can remain as background lighting, while a compatible smart bulb can return to an everyday white-light setting.Before packing away the decorations, review festive schedules and disable unnecessary routines. The same setup can then move from a seasonal display to lighting for evenings, meals or family gatherings.
Article Summary: Diwali lighting should have a purpose. For a compact flat, start with one illuminated entrance, one softly lit gathering space, and one decorative highlight. Smart lights add control to that setup, letting compatible bulbs and strips change brightness, colour, or operating hours.

Article Title: Snowflake launches AI Agent innovations to power the Agentic Enterprise at Expedition 2026

Snowflake announces core innovations

AI Data Cloud company Snowflake has announced a major expansion of its product suite at Snowflake Expedition 2026, positioning its platform as the foundational control and governance layer for enterprise-ready AI agents. The announcements target the primary friction point preventing companies from scaling autonomous systems: enterprise trust.According to a recent MIT Technology Review report sponsored by Snowflake, 55% of executives cite a lack of business context as the chief driver of low-quality AI agent insights, while 45% point to fragmented or inaccessible data. To bridge this gap, Snowflake is combining approved enterprise context, unified governance and autonomous execution into a single, cohesive architecture.Integrated into Snowflake Horizon Catalog, Business Ontology allows organisations to assign accountable owners to core business definitions (e.g., net revenue), link definitions directly to underlying data, and log changes for auditability. Supported by Semantic Views for calculation and Cortex Sense for inferring undefined concepts, it ensures AI agents deliver consistent, approved business metrics rather than unverified approximations.This acts as a centralised governance gate for all agent operations across multi-cloud environments, frameworks and AI providers. Key mechanisms include:This service connects to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, enforcing existing human access permissions, authentication and authorisation rules on agent actions.Inspects tool calls against fine-grained authorisation policies and filters for prompt injections or jailbreaks.Records end-to-end execution steps directly into the customer’s Snowflake account for analysis via Agent Trace Intelligence, while Agent Abuse Detection monitors overall agent trajectories for abnormal behaviour.Enforces hard spend limits, tracks compute spend at the department or agent level, and uses Dynamic Model Routing to route routine tasks to smaller, cost-optimized models.Agentic apps designed to automate routine business workflows. While Snowflake CoCo is a dedicated coding agent tailored for data engineering and data teams, Snowflake CoWork is a personal productivity and work agent built for knowledge workers.Always-on background instances (CoCo Bots and CoWork Bots) that work directly inside day-to-day enterprise tools, escalating to human users only when formal approvals or decisions are required.
Article Summary: Data Cloud company Snowflake has announced a major expansion of its product suite. The announcements target the primary friction point preventing companies from scaling autonomous systems. Snowflake is combining approved enterprise context, unified governance and autonomous execution into a single, cohesive architecture.

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. When connected to a 350kW DC fast charger, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes.ID@undefined Caption not available.Built on Jaguar's new Electric Architecture (JEA), the Type 01 has been designed to offer a balance of performance and comfort. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
